title: False friends for Spanish speakers
description: 40 palabras que parecen españolas pero significan otra cosa. La definición y la traducción dan el significado REAL; el aviso, la trampa.

cards.definition: In fact; really (often correcting an idea).
cards.example: Many people think the policy failed, but actually it reduced traffic by 15%.
cards.warning: NO significa 'actualmente'. 'Actualmente' = currently / at present / nowadays.

cards.definition: In the end, after a long time.
cards.example: After years of debate, the city eventually banned cars from the centre.
cards.warning: NO significa 'eventualmente' (= posiblemente, ocasionalmente). Eso es 'possibly' / 'occasionally'.

cards.example: It would be sensible to invest in public transport before building more roads.
cards.warning: NO es 'sensible' en español. 'Sensible' (emocional) = sensitive.

cards.definition: Easily affected or upset; needing careful handling.
cards.example: Immigration is a sensitive issue in many countries.
cards.warning: Es la traducción de 'sensible' en español. No confundir con 'sensible' (sensato).

cards.example: I was embarrassed when I forgot my teacher's name.
cards.warning: NO es 'embarazada' (= pregnant). Error clásico y muy visible.

cards.definition: The series of jobs in a person's working life.
cards.example: She built a successful career in engineering.
cards.warning: NO es la 'carrera' universitaria (= degree). 'Estudio la carrera de Derecho' = I'm doing a law degree.

cards.example: Volunteers assist elderly residents with their shopping.
cards.warning: NO es 'asistir a clase' (= attend). 'I assisted the lecture' es incorrecto.

cards.definition: To be present at an event or go regularly to a place.
cards.example: Over 90% of children attend primary school in the region.
cards.warning: NO es 'atender' (= serve / pay attention / look after); ojo: 'attend TO someone/something' sí es 'atender, ocuparse de'. Para 'asistir', sin preposición: 'attend a class', no 'attend to a class'.

cards.example: The hotel rooms have a soft carpet and large windows.
cards.warning: NO es 'carpeta' (= folder / file).

cards.definition: A place where you can borrow or read books.
cards.example: The university library is open 24 hours during exam period.
cards.warning: NO es 'librería' (= bookshop / bookstore).

cards.definition: Unable to empty the bowels easily.
cards.example: A diet low in fibre can make people constipated.
cards.warning: NO es 'constipado' (= have a cold). Di 'I have a cold'.

cards.example: I didn't realise how expensive the city was until I moved there.
cards.warning: NO es 'realizar' en el sentido de hacer (= carry out / do / make): 'carry out a project', no 'realise a project'. Sólo coinciden en 'realise a dream / your potential' (= hacer realidad).

cards.definition: To act as if something is true when it is not.
cards.example: Some students pretend to understand rather than ask questions.
cards.warning: NO es 'pretender' (= intend / aim / try). 'I pretend to study medicine' significa que finges.

cards.definition: To plan or mean to do something.
cards.example: I intend to apply for a master's degree next year.
cards.warning: Es la traducción correcta de 'pretender'.

cards.example: Please use the nearest emergency exit.
cards.warning: NO es 'éxito' (= success).

cards.example: The success of the scheme depends on public support.
cards.warning: NO es 'suceso' (= event / incident).

cards.definition: A person injured or killed in an accident or war.
cards.example: There were no casualties in the train accident.
cards.warning: NO es 'casualidad' (= coincidence / chance).

cards.example: Many tech companies have a casual dress code.
cards.warning: Normalmente NO es 'casual' en español (= by chance / coincidental): 'fue casualidad' = 'it was a coincidence'. Sólo se acercan en usos como 'a casual remark' (comentario hecho sin pensar).

cards.example: The actual cost of the project was twice the estimate.
cards.warning: NO es 'actual' (= current / present).

cards.example: The current system of university funding is unsustainable.
cards.warning: Es la traducción de 'actual'. También: present, today's.

cards.definition: 1) A reason supporting an idea. 2) An angry disagreement.
cards.example: My parents had an argument about money.
cards.warning: Ojo: también significa 'pelea'. 'Argumento' de una película = plot.

cards.definition: A calm conversation about a topic.
cards.example: The class had an interesting discussion about climate policy.
cards.warning: NO es 'discusión' en el sentido de pelea (= argument / row).

cards.definition: Showing understanding and care for someone's problems.
cards.example: My manager was very sympathetic when my father was ill.
cards.warning: NO es 'simpático' (= nice / friendly / likeable).

cards.example: She is a highly educated woman with two PhDs.
cards.warning: NO es 'educado' (= polite / well-mannered).

cards.example: I'm really excited about my trip to Canada.
cards.warning: NO es 'excitante / excitado' (en español suelen sonar a agitación o connotación sexual). En inglés es lo normal para 'ilusión / entusiasmo'.

cards.definition: A raw material or product that is bought and sold.
cards.example: Coffee is one of the most traded commodities in the world.
cards.warning: NO es 'comodidad' (= comfort / convenience).

cards.example: The report offers a comprehensive analysis of the housing market.
cards.warning: NO es 'comprensivo' (= understanding / sympathetic).

cards.example: The first lecture of the course is on Monday at 9.
cards.warning: NO es 'lectura' (= reading).

cards.example: Many young adults now live with their parents until their thirties.
cards.warning: NO es 'parientes' (= relatives).

cards.example: Cotton is a light, breathable fabric.
cards.warning: NO es 'fábrica' (= factory).

cards.example: My tutor gave me some useful advice about the essay.
cards.warning: NO es 'aviso' (= warning / notice). 'Advice' es incontable: 'a piece of advice', nunca 'an advice'.

cards.example: Classes will resume after the holiday.
cards.warning: NO es 'resumir' (= summarise). Y 'résumé' (US) = currículum.

cards.definition: To help, encourage or agree with.
cards.example: Most citizens support the new recycling law.
cards.warning: NO es 'soportar' en el sentido de aguantar algo molesto (= stand / put up with / bear): 'I can't support noise' → 'I can't stand noise'. Sí coincide en sentido físico: 'the columns support the roof'.

cards.definition: To store sound or information; a written account.
cards.example: The lectures are recorded so students can watch them later.
cards.warning: NO es 'recordar' (= remember / remind).

cards.definition: To attack or abuse someone sexually.
cards.example: Sorry to bother you, but could you help me? (NOT: Sorry to molest you.)
cards.warning: NO es 'molestar' (= bother / disturb / annoy). Error muy grave.

cards.definition: A chemical that keeps food fresh.
cards.example: Many processed foods contain artificial preservatives.
cards.warning: NO es 'preservativo' (= condom).

cards.definition: A subject of discussion or writing.
cards.example: The essay topic was the role of museums in society.
cards.warning: NO es 'tópico' (= cliché / stereotype).

cards.definition: The act of tricking or lying.
cards.example: The advert was banned for deception.
cards.warning: NO es 'decepción' (= disappointment).

cards.example: She won a national photography contest.
cards.warning: NO es 'contestar' (= answer / reply).

cards.example: A large proportion of the budget goes on healthcare.
cards.warning: NO es 'largo' (= long).

title: Key collocations
description: 30 combinaciones verbo + sustantivo (make, do, take, have, pay, raise…) que los hispanohablantes suelen traducir mal.

cards.example: Governments must make difficult decisions about public spending.
cards.warning: No 'take a decision' (posible en UK pero menos común) ni 'do a decision'.

cards.definition: To study a subject in detail.
cards.example: Scientists are doing research into new vaccines.
cards.warning: 'research' es incontable: 'do research', no 'make a research' ni 'researches'.

cards.definition: To watch, listen or think carefully.
cards.example: Drivers who use phones do not pay attention to the road.
cards.warning: No 'put attention' ni 'lend attention'.

cards.example: Everyone makes mistakes when learning a language.
cards.warning: No 'do a mistake' ni 'commit a mistake'.

cards.example: I'm taking the IELTS exam in June.
cards.warning: No 'make an exam'. 'Pass an exam' = aprobar (no 'hacer').

cards.example: Children in some countries do two hours of homework a night.
cards.warning: No 'make homework'. 'Homework' es incontable.

cards.example: She has made great progress in her speaking.
cards.warning: No 'do progress'. 'progress' es incontable: no 'a progress'.

cards.example: Citizens should make an effort to reduce waste.
cards.warning: No 'do an effort'.

cards.example: The festival takes place every August.
cards.warning: Intransitivo y sin pasiva: no 'was taken place'.

cards.definition: To use an opportunity; to exploit unfairly.
cards.example: Students should take advantage of free online courses.
cards.warning: No 'take profit of' ni 'profit the opportunity'.

cards.example: Over 500 volunteers took part in the study.
cards.warning: Preposición 'in', no 'of' ni 'on'.

cards.example: Social media has a huge impact on young people's self-esteem.
cards.warning: Preposición 'on', no 'in' ni 'over'.

cards.definition: To be involved in or contribute to.
cards.example: Parents play a key role in children's education.
cards.warning: No 'have a role' (posible pero menos natural) ni 'make a role'.

cards.definition: To make people know more about an issue.
cards.example: Campaigns can raise awareness of the dangers of smoking.
cards.warning: No 'rise awareness' ('rise' es intransitivo) ni 'make conscious'.

cards.example: The city cannot build houses fast enough to meet demand.
cards.warning: 'Satisfy demand' es posible, pero 'meet' es lo más natural; evita 'cover the needs' (calco).

cards.es: llegar a un acuerdo / a una conclusión
cards.example: The two sides failed to reach an agreement.
cards.warning: No 'arrive to an agreement'.

cards.example: Young people who commit minor crimes need support, not just punishment.
cards.warning: 'commit' va con delitos y actos graves (a crime, an offence, fraud, murder); para errores normales es 'make a mistake'.

cards.definition: To deal with or find an answer to a problem.
cards.example: Governments must tackle the problem of youth unemployment.
cards.warning: No 'give a solution to the problem' (calco); mejor 'find a solution to'.

cards.definition: To decide something based on evidence.
cards.example: It is difficult to draw firm conclusions from such a small study.
cards.warning: No 'take a conclusion' ni 'extract a conclusion'.

cards.definition: To get money from work or business.
cards.example: Many students work part-time to earn money for rent.
cards.warning: No 'win money' (= ganar en un juego o premio).

cards.example: Plastic waste does enormous damage to marine life.
cards.warning: No 'make damage'. 'damage' es incontable en este sentido.

cards.example: Could you do me a favour and check my essay?
cards.warning: No 'make a favour'.

cards.example: Let's have a look at the figures for 2020.
cards.warning: No 'give a look' ni 'throw a look'.

cards.es: hacer una presentación / dar un discurso
cards.example: Every student has to give a ten-minute presentation.
cards.warning: No 'make a presentation' (posible en negocios) y nunca 'do a speech'.

cards.definition: To put a question to someone.
cards.example: Don't be afraid to ask questions in class.
cards.warning: No 'make a question' (calco directo del español).

cards.definition: To act to deal with a problem.
cards.example: Authorities must take urgent measures to reduce air pollution.
cards.warning: No 'make measures' ni 'adopt actions' (calco).

cards.es: suponer una amenaza / un riesgo para
cards.example: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal cities.
cards.warning: No 'suppose a threat' ('suppose' = suponer en el sentido de imaginar).

cards.example: My aunt has run a small restaurant for twenty years.
cards.warning: No 'carry a business' ni 'lead a business' (lead = liderar, distinto matiz).

cards.term: heavy traffic / heavy rain / strong coffee
cards.definition: Natural adjective + noun pairs for intensity.
cards.es: tráfico denso / lluvia fuerte / café cargado
cards.example: Heavy traffic adds an hour to my commute every day.
cards.warning: No 'strong rain' ni 'big traffic'. Tampoco 'heavy coffee'.

cards.term: high / low + level, rate, price, cost
cards.definition: Use high/low (not big/small) with these nouns.
cards.es: nivel / tasa / precio alto o bajo
cards.example: High levels of unemployment can lead to social unrest.
cards.warning: No 'big prices' ni 'expensive prices' (los precios no son caros; las cosas sí).

title: Preposition traps
description: 30 verbos, adjetivos y sustantivos con la preposición que los hispanohablantes suelen fallar. El aviso muestra la forma incorrecta.

cards.definition: To be determined by; to rely on.
cards.example: Success depends on hard work as much as talent.
cards.warning: ✗ depend of

cards.example: She is married to a doctor. He married his classmate.
cards.warning: ✗ married with someone ✗ marry with someone ('married with two children' sí existe: casado y con dos hijos)

cards.example: Young people are increasingly interested in sustainable fashion.
cards.warning: ✗ interested on ✗ interested for

cards.example: We arrived in Tokyo at night and arrived at the hotel at midnight.
cards.warning: ✗ arrive to (salvo en algunos usos US). Y 'arrive home' sin preposición.

cards.example: The course consists of ten modules.
cards.warning: ✗ consist in (existe pero significa otra cosa, 'radicar en') ✗ is consisted of

cards.definition: To consider / have an opinion about.
cards.example: What do you think of the new policy? I'm thinking about changing jobs.
cards.warning: ✗ think in (calco de 'pensar en')

cards.example: Many children dream of becoming astronauts.
cards.warning: ✗ dream with

cards.example: I've never been good at maths.
cards.warning: ✗ good in ✗ good on

cards.definition: Having the duty to deal with; being the cause of.
cards.example: Cars are responsible for a large share of urban emissions.
cards.warning: ✗ responsible of

cards.example: Life in the countryside is very different from life in the city.
cards.warning: ✗ different of. ('different to' es aceptable en UK; 'different than' en US).

cards.example: The Spanish system is similar to the French one.
cards.warning: ✗ similar of ✗ similar than

cards.definition: To pay attention to a sound.
cards.example: I listen to podcasts on my way to work.
cards.warning: ✗ listen music (falta 'to')

cards.example: If you don't understand, ask for help.
cards.warning: ✗ ask help ✗ ask to the teacher (se dice 'ask the teacher')

cards.example: Patients often wait for months for an operation.
cards.warning: ✗ wait someone ✗ wait to someone

cards.definition: To give money in exchange for something.
cards.example: Who should pay for university education?
cards.warning: ✗ pay the dinner (se dice 'pay for the dinner'; pero 'pay the bill')

cards.example: Visitors must show ID to enter the building.
cards.warning: ✗ enter in / enter into the building

cards.example: This essay will discuss the benefits of remote work.
cards.warning: ✗ discuss about (pero 'a discussion about' sí)

cards.definition: To make something clear to a person.
cards.example: Can you explain the rules to me?
cards.warning: ✗ explain me the rules

cards.definition: 'with' a person/opinion, 'on' a topic, 'to' a proposal.
cards.es: estar de acuerdo con / en; aceptar
cards.example: I completely agree with this view.
cards.warning: ✗ I am agree ✗ agree to someone

cards.example: In my opinion, public transport should be free.
cards.warning: ✗ on my opinion ✗ for my opinion. Y no 'In my opinion, I think...' (redundante).

cards.example: Cities offer jobs; on the other hand, they are expensive.
cards.warning: ✗ in the other hand ✗ by the other hand

cards.example: I usually go hiking at the weekend.
cards.warning: ✗ in the weekend

cards.term: in the morning / at night / on Monday
cards.es: por la mañana / por la noche / el lunes
cards.example: I study best in the morning and on Sundays.
cards.warning: ✗ in the night (salvo 'durante la noche') ✗ in Monday ✗ at the morning

cards.term: an increase in / a rise in
cards.example: There has been an increase in obesity among children.
cards.warning: ✗ an increase of obesity (use 'of' sólo para la cantidad: 'an increase of 5%')

cards.term: the reason for / the cause of
cards.es: la razón de / la causa de
cards.example: The main reason for the decline is cheaper competition.
cards.warning: ✗ the reason of ✗ the cause for the decline ('cause for concern' = motivo de preocupación sí existe)

cards.example: There is no simple solution to traffic congestion.
cards.warning: ✗ a solution for (menos natural) ✗ a solution of

cards.definition: What something does to another thing.
cards.example: Screen time has a negative effect on sleep.
cards.warning: ✗ effect in ✗ influence in

cards.example: Many parents are worried about online safety.
cards.warning: ✗ worried for (salvo personas en peligro) ✗ afraid to the dark

cards.example: My region is famous for its olive oil.
cards.warning: ✗ famous by ✗ known by (que significa otra cosa: 'conocido con el nombre de')

cards.definition: To use money / time for something.
cards.es: gastar dinero en / pasar tiempo haciendo
cards.example: Teenagers spend too much time scrolling and too much money on clothes.
cards.warning: ✗ spend money in clothes ✗ spend time to study ('spend money in shops' sí, porque indica el lugar)
